links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness of DL opportunistic screening across osteoporosis prevalence settings
links.effect: DL screening was cost-effective versus no screening only when osteoporosis prevalence exceeded 14.3%; the base-case ICER was 21,827 per QALY.
links.quote: The approach became cost-effective when osteoporosis prevalence exceeded 14.3%.

links.outcome: Cost-effectiveness under varying confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation completion rates
links.effect: Cost-effective with full care-pathway completion (ICER 21,827 per QALY); not maintained under real-world confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation rates observed in Taiwan.
links.quote: Its value depended on disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and completion of confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation, and was not maintained under real-world examination estimates observed in Taiwan.
